messages.author: 276885ca8ae451fe
messages.subject: MRDS perpendicular distance
parts:
Dear All,



Please would clear this up from me. I have double platform, trial
configuration data for common dolphins, which I'm analysing with MRDS in
Distance 6. Which perpendicular range should I use for duplicate trials -
Obs1 (primary platform) or Obs2 (tracker platform who set the trials)? I
understand that I should enter the same distance for both data sheet rows
for the same object.



I began with some CDS exploration of the Obs1 data, looking at truncation,
interval bins, and then model selection. Then I moved on to the MRDS full
independence fitting method. My understanding was that as I was using the
Obs1 data in the DS part of the model, I should use the these ranges for
Obs1 sightings including the duplicates. But, if a mixture of Obs1 ranges
(duplicates) and Obs2 ranges (unsuccessful trials) were used in the MRDS
part of the model, to model the conditional detection function, wouldn't
there be a bias towards ranges closer to the vessel - duplicates would
likely have smaller ranges than unsuccessful Obs2 trials?



Alternatively, how could I use the Obs2 ranges for the duplicates - there
was a reduction in range between the initial (or even last re-sighted)
tracker range and the Obs1 range, so this would skew the distribution of
ranges to the right? I guess I should use the last re-sighting range rather
than the initial range perhaps.



I'm sure there's a simple answer to this - please excuse my lack of
understanding, I couldn't find the answer in the standard texts or Distance
help.



Thanks,



Chris

messages.author: 5140016d70f6ba82
messages.subject: Re: MRDS perpendicular distance
parts:
On 9/12/2011 8:36 AM, Chris Pierpoint wrote:
> > Dear All,
> >
> >
> >
> > Please would clear this up from me. I have double platform, trial
> > configuration data for common dolphins, which I'm analysing with MRDS in
> > Distance 6. Which perpendicular range should I use for duplicate trials -
> > Obs1 (primary platform) or Obs2 (tracker platform who set the trials)? I
> > understand that I should enter the same distance for both data sheet rows
> > for the same object.

What do you mean by perpendicular range? Do you mean what do you set
for the transect (half-)width?

> >
> >
> >
> > I began with some CDS exploration of the Obs1 data, looking at truncation,
> > interval bins, and then model selection. Then I moved on to the MRDS full
> > independence fitting method. My understanding was that as I was using the
> > Obs1 data in the DS part of the model, I should use the these ranges for
> > Obs1 sightings including the duplicates. But, if a mixture of Obs1 ranges
> > (duplicates) and Obs2 ranges (unsuccessful trials) were used in the MRDS
> > part of the model, to model the conditional detection function, wouldn't
> > there be a bias towards ranges closer to the vessel - duplicates would
> > likely have smaller ranges than unsuccessful Obs2 trials?

You need to understand that the full independence models currently in
mrds do not fit a detection model based on distance sampling. They
solely use the conditional detection function which for the trial
configuration would use obs2 data as trials and would estimate the
detection function of obs1 from the missed/seen by obs1. For the trial
configuration, the full independence model is simply a logistic
regression. It uses the distances from observer 2 for the trials and
they would be used for the range (width if that is what you mean).

> >
> >
> >
> > Alternatively, how could I use the Obs2 ranges for the duplicates - there
> > was a reduction in range between the initial (or even last re-sighted)
> > tracker range and the Obs1 range, so this would skew the distribution of
> > ranges to the right? I guess I should use the last re-sighting range rather
> > than the initial range perhaps.

Presumably this is why you are using trial full independence because the
dolphins are being attracted to the boat. You should use the distance
of the initial sighting by observer 2. It is for these kind of
circumstances that the trial full independence model is useful. As you
noted the distances are smaller for observer 1 who is seeing them
sometimes after they have been attracted to the vessel, which is why
those distances are not used in the estimation of obs1 detection
function. See Buckland S.T., Turnock B.J. (1992) A robust line transect
method. Biometrics 48:901-909

regards --jeff
